full_judgment:
Mustafa Kamal, J.—This rule was obtained by the petitioner under Article 102(2) of the suspended Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh as restored under the Constitution (Partial Revival) (Second) Order, 1985 read with the Proclamation Order No. 1 of 1985 calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned order of cancellation of licence (Annexure-G) as contained in Memo No. DA/U-19/84/1950 dated 17.4.1983 under the signature of the respondent No. 1 the Director, Drug Administration and Licensing Authority (Drugs). Directorate of Drug Administration should not be declared to have been passed without any lawful authority and of no legal effect. 

 4. Thereafter it is the petitioner's case that a false drug case was instituted against him under the said Ordinance in which he was acquitted. The photocopy of the judgment is Annexure D. The petitioner is now being proceeded against in a second drug care and during the pendency of the second drug case be received an order of cancellation of the unani drug manufacturing licence of his firm under the signature of the respondent No. 1 bearing Memo No. DA/U-19/94/1950 dated 14.4.85 a photocopy of which Is Annexere E. This is the order under challenge.
